trust_decision.summary: A frontmatter value of the form ${file:<path>} is expanded by joining the prompt file's directory with the attacker-controlled remainder (no canonicalization, no containment check) and then read from disk, so '../' or an absolute path makes the loader read any file the process can read; the decision is per-runtime in each loader's reference resolver (Rust resolve_file, Python _pre_process, C# ReferenceResolver.ResolveFileRef, TS makePreProcess), and the published fix adds a canonical-path containment check against the prompt directory plus host-supplied allowed roots at all four.

landing_point.why: The task's language is Rust and this one line (agent_dir.join(relative_path) followed immediately by fs::read_to_string) is the whole of '${file:...} expansion' in the Rust runtime, so a report about arbitrary file read via file references lands here first.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and the Rust task name one runtime, and Python, C# and TypeScript each ship a complete independent loader in a different package and language, so fixing only resolve_file in the Rust crate reads as a complete fix; the same reasoning is available for PromptyTool child paths, which are a documented child-agent feature rather than ${file:...} expansion.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Out-of-tree file references that a host legitimately relies on must keep working: the published fix's own allowed-roots exception is the requirement, and the repo already resolves references against a base that is not the prompt directory (the C# spec-vector harness resolves inline frontmatter with parentDir ".", i.e. the process CWD, and the fix has to pass the CWD as an allowed root to keep that green). An over-broad fix that rejects every absolute path or every '..' outright, instead of canonicalizing and then testing containment against prompt-dir-plus-host-roots, breaks the documented shared connection-file pattern (a shared/ JSON next to a prompts/ tree) and that harness.

O6_input_shapes: relative reference containing '..' segments that escape the prompt directory (${file:../secret.txt})
absolute path reference outside the prompt directory (${file:/etc/passwd} style, accepted by Path.Combine / Path.join / resolve / '/')
reference to a symlink that lives inside the prompt directory but whose final target is outside it (needs to-final canonicalization of both target and roots, not just lexically)
reference that stays inside the prompt directory, including subdirectories, which must still resolve
optional host-supplied extra roots (allowed_file_roots / AllowedFileRoots / allowedFileRoots / LoadOptions) that make an otherwise-outside reference legal
